_README: What each committee normally buys. EDIT THIS FILE, not Python.
The spend review reads this to decide which purchases get a friendly
'can you tell us what this was for?' note. It never changes a category and
never decides anything on its own -- a treasurer reads every flag.
Each committee lists merchant TYPES (defined under merchant_types below) at
expected     : routine for this committee. No note.
ask          : can be fine, but we would like a one-line reason.
not_allowed  : outside policy. Always reviewed by the treasurer.
A type a committee does not list falls back to `default_level`. Org-wide
levels under `everyone` override a committee's own list.
DRAFT 2026-10-02, built from 611 card purchases (Supabase, May 2022 - Jan
2026, plus the Fall 2026 statement). 'History' notes count past purchases
per type; a type used often is 'expected' unless it is a known risk.
Keys beginning with an underscore are ignored.

_review_window: Only purchases from the last 12 months are reviewed. Older history is settled (treasurer, 2026-10-02) and is used only to learn what is normal.
_event_types: Store types that mean 'an event happened'. A committee marked events_belong_elsewhere gets a note on these that suggests which committee usually pays for that kind of spending.

small_ok_under._why: Below these amounts a store type is fine for any committee: a few dollars at a gas station is ice or snacks for an event (treasurer, 2026-10-02).

_comment: Checks that do not depend on the merchant type. Each produces a note at the given level.
Only CATEGORIZED rows are reviewed: an uncategorized row is the categorizer's
job first. Lessons from the dry run (2026-10-02) are folded in below.

missing_receipt.why: Over receipt_required_over with no receipt attached. Over large_purchase_over, the receipt should also name the event. A large purchase WITH a receipt gets no note: big socials are routine.

unknown_card.why: Card is not on card_roster.json for this period.

outside_term.why: Dated between terms, when no committee events are scheduled.

recurring_charge.why: Same merchant and amount in recurring_min_count or more DIFFERENT MONTHS, at or over recurring_min_amount. Count across all rows, categorized or not. Same-day repeats are a group tab, not a subscription. Software is exempt.

same_day_split.why: Several charges at one merchant on one day that together pass receipt_required_over: one note for the group, asking for the receipt.

transfer_to_individual.why: Zelle/Venmo out to a person with no matching reimbursement request.

card_committee_mismatch.why: Bought on a card the roster assigns to one committee but booked to another. Either the booking is wrong, or one committee covered for another (often a card gap at the start of a term). Shown grouped by card, not row by row.

ticketed_outing.why: Activities & entertainment over ticketed_outing_over (theme parks, escape rooms...). Often members pay part back, so the note asks whether they did and points at their payments to match. Flagged even when the outing itself is normal for the committee (treasurer, 2026-10-02: Busch Gardens).

before_card_issued.why: For a committee marked events_belong_elsewhere: if the suggested committee's current card had not been used yet on that date, the note says so -- the usual reason the spending landed on the wrong budget.

rules._rejected: Large purchases alone are NOT flagged when the store type is expected for the committee: bar tabs at Arcade Bar or The Backyard are what Membership spends on (treasurer, 2026-10-02).
